messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> P1: high error rate (502/503) for customer 'OrionFin' on private VPC ingress. Observed from 2219876500. Affects dedicated pool orion-prod-1 behind NLB 'orion-nlb-ingress'. Please ack and join.

sam: acked. I'm oncall. first pass: checking LB health checks + target group.

emily: seeing a big spike in failed health checks for targets in tg-orion-app (503). CloudWatch shows health check failures started ~ 2219876400.

javier: any recent deploys to orion-prod-1?

emily: no deploys in the last 6h. but there was an automated security group sync at 2200Z that touched tenant SGs — investigating if that mutated a rule.

maya: customer says they started seeing 502s at ~2208Z, matches. customer-ops: can you confirm any firewall changes on your side?

customer-ops: nothing on our side. we did rotate our upstream firewall keys earlier but didn't change IP allowlist.

sam: ok. hypothesis: NLB health checks are failing because source IPs for health checks are being blocked by a recently tightened SG rule. If targets fail health checks, NLB returns 502/503. emily, can you confirm SG Eval?

emily: running a quick check. Found a deny that drops 10.0.0.0/8 -> target SG (sg-orion-app) for tcp/443 (CIDR deny added by automation). That would block internal healthcheck traffic from our healthchecker subnet 10.0.2.0/24.

javier: confirmed. health checks originate from eni subnets in the same VPC 10.0.2.0/24. automation rule pr-7892 mistakenly added a more restrictive egress/ingress rule.

sam: impact: targets marked unhealthy -> NLB returns 502 for client requests. Mitigation: add temporary allow for healthcheck CIDR to target SG and cloud-internal sources. We'll need to do this with minimal blast radius.

emily: ready to apply. planned command (one-liner):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-orion-app --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.0.2.0/24 --region us-west-2
```

nidhi: add logging rule too so we can revert safely. Also tag the change with incident id.

maya: can we also change NLB health check port to 8080 temporarily (app still serves on 8080) while we validate? less risky than broad SG change.

emily: app responds on 8080, yes. but LB healthchecks are configured for 443/https with TLS. if we flip to 8080/http we avoid TLS termination differences. I'll update TG health check to http:8080, interval 10s, unhealthy threshold 2.

sam: plan: (1) add SG allow 10.0.2.0/24:443 (2) change TG health check to http:8080 (3) observe health checks return healthy (4) revert SG automation change after verified.

customer-ops: while you do that, our users are seeing intermittent failures. any ETA?

sam: target is to have healthchecks healthy within 5m of the SG rule applied + healthcheck change. I'll call it T+5m after change for updates.

emily: applying SG rule now (will tag with Incident-2219876543).

emily: done. output:
```
{ "Return": true, "RequestId": "req-abcdef" }
```

emily: updating TG health check to http:8080 now.

javier: showing first successful healthcheck 10s after change for 3/6 targets.

sam: good. monitor logs and client error rate. can we run a curl from inside the VPC to each target on 8080?

emily: running curl sweep:
```
for ip in $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=orion-app" --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].PrivateIpAddress' --output text); do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" http://$ip:8080/health || echo $ip fail; done
```

emily: results: 200 from all 6 targets.

javier: NLB target health goes to healthy for all targets within 30s.

sam: customer, can you validate traffic now?

customer-ops: just checked: requests from our side look normal, errors dropped to 1% from 45%. thanks.

nidhi: we should still revert the automation rule that removed internal CIDRs from sg-orion-app. propose: update automation PR to exclude the mgmt/healthcheck CIDRs, then redeploy. Also add a unit test for allowlist exceptions.

emily: creating rollback PR and tagging sec-team for postmortem.

maya: ops note for postmortem: tighten review on infra syncs that change tenant SGs. Also add explicit healthcheck allowlist in the runbook.

sam: summary: root cause - infra automation tightened SGs and removed internal healthcheck CIDR; symptom - NLB marked targets unhealthy leading to 502/503 for customer on dedicated pool; mitigation - temporary SG ingress rule + change TG healthcheck to http:8080; verified healthy and customer confirms reduced errors. Next steps: revert automation properly, code fix in PR #4021, postmortem runbook and customer RCA.

incident-bot: Incident 2219876543 -> resolved (mitigation applied). Please proceed with postmortem template and follow-up actions. :white_check_mark:

sam: wrapping up, will follow up with an RCA doc and schedule a customer post-call. thanks all for quick responses.
